tool.name: LCA with FishBase
tool.description: assign taxonomy to eDNA sequences from BLAST hits
tool.command: ## The script looks in ./cache before any download and uses a cached file when it exists, ## so the reference files are placed there and the job needs no network access. mkdir -p cache/taxdump && ln -s '${taxonomy.fields.path}/nodes.dmp' cache/taxdump/nodes.dmp && ln -s '${taxonomy.fields.path}/names.dmp' cache/taxdump/names.dmp && ln -s '$fishbase_species' cache/fishbase_species.parquet && ln -s '$fishbase_families' cache/fishbase_families.parquet && ln -s '$fishbase_synonyms' cache/fishbase_synonyms.parquet && ln -s '$worms' worms_species.txt && python '$__tool_directory__/calculateLCAWithFishbase_Claude_FAIReCompatible.py' -f '$blast_results' --asv_table '$asv_table' -o lca_output.tsv --raw_output taxaRaw.tsv --final_output taxaFinal.tsv --missing_out missing.csv --worms_file worms_species.txt --pident $pident --min_coverage $min_coverage --cutoff $cutoff $use_bitwise $normalise_identity --log_level $log_level && ## the script writes no output when no hit passes the filters if [ ! -s lca_output.tsv ]; then echo 'No BLAST hit passed the identity and coverage filters, so there is no LCA to report' >&2; exit 1; fi && ## Nextflow (LCA_WITH_FISHBASE) removes the quotes from the two FAIRe tables sed 's/"//g' taxaRaw.tsv > taxa_raw.tsv && sed 's/"//g' taxaFinal.tsv > taxa_final.tsv

param.name: blast_results
param.label: BLAST table
param.help: BLAST tabular output with the 22 columns qseqid sseqid staxids sscinames scomnames sskingdoms pident length qlen slen mismatch gapopen gaps qstart qend sstart send stitle evalue bitscore qcovs qcovhsp, in this order

param.name: asv_table
param.label: ASV table with sequences
param.help: Read counts per sample. First column: the sequence name as in the BLAST table (ASV); last column: the sequence (ASV_sequence); a header line

param.name: taxonomy
param.label: NCBI taxonomy
param.help: A copy of the NCBI taxonomy (nodes.dmp and names.dmp) installed on this Galaxy. Use a copy from March 2025 or later: the script reads the rank 'domain', which NCBI introduced then; with an older copy every domain is 'Unknown'

validator.message: No NCBI taxonomy is installed on this Galaxy. Ask the administrator to run the NCBI taxonomy data manager

param.name: fishbase_species
param.label: FishBase species table
param.help: File species.parquet of a FishBase release (for example v24.07 from huggingface.co/datasets/cboettig/fishbase)

param.name: fishbase_families
param.label: FishBase families table
param.help: File families.parquet of the same FishBase release

param.name: fishbase_synonyms
param.label: FishBase synonyms table
param.help: File synonyms.parquet of the same FishBase release

param.name: worms
param.label: WoRMS species file
param.help: Tab-separated, no header, 10 columns (species, genus, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, unused, epithet), as worms_species.txt in the LCA_With_Fishbase repository

param.label: Minimum percent identity
param.help: BLAST hits below this identity are not used

param.label: Minimum query coverage (percent)
param.help: BLAST hits with a lower query coverage (qcovs) are not used

param.label: Identity window (percentage points)
param.help: At each rank, the hits within this many percentage points of the top hit decide the assignment. Hits that agree give a name; hits that disagree give 'dropped'

param.label: Rank the hits by bit score
param.help: Yes: the top hit is the hit with the highest bit score. No: the top hit is the hit with the highest percent identity

param.label: Normalise identity by query coverage
param.help: Multiplies the percent identity of each hit by its query coverage before the comparison

tool.help:
**What it does**
Assigns a taxonomic name to each sequence (ASV, ZOTU or OTU) from its BLAST hits, by the lowest common ancestor (LCA) method of the OceanOmics amplicon pipeline (Minderoo Foundation OceanOmics Centre). It is the script *calculateLCAWithFishbase_Claude_FAIReCompatible.py* of the pipeline, release 1.3.4, unchanged except one comment line that the style check needs.
For each sequence:
1. BLAST hits below the minimum identity or the minimum query coverage are removed. 2. Each remaining hit gets a lineage (domain to species). A hit with an NCBI taxonomy ID gets its lineage from the NCBI taxonomy; for a fish, the genus and family come from FishBase when the genus is there, then from WoRMS. A hit without a taxonomy ID (N/A or 0) is named from FishBase or WoRMS by the genus name in the hit title. A hit with no lineage is skipped. 3. One hit per taxonomy ID is kept. The hits are ranked by bit score (default) or by percent identity. 4. At each rank, from domain to species, the hits within the identity window of the top hit are compared. If they agree, the name is assigned; if they do not, the rank is "dropped".
**Inputs**
- BLAST table: tabular output of blastn with these 22 columns in this order: qseqid sseqid staxids sscinames scomnames sskingdoms pident length qlen slen mismatch gapopen gaps qstart qend sstart send stitle evalue bitscore qcovs qcovhsp. - ASV table with sequences: one row per sequence; first column the sequence name as in the BLAST table, then one column per sample with read counts, last column the sequence. - NCBI taxonomy: a copy installed on this Galaxy (data table *ncbi_taxonomy*). Use a copy from March 2025 or later, because the script reads the rank "domain". - FishBase tables: the files *species.parquet*, *families.parquet* and *synonyms.parquet* of one FishBase release, for example v24.07 from https://huggingface.co/datasets/cboettig/fishbase (folder data/fb/v24.07/parquet). The pipeline uses v24.07. - WoRMS species file: *worms_species.txt.gz* from https://github.com/Minderoo-OceanOmics-Centre-UWA/LCA_With_Fishbase (folder data), uploaded to Galaxy (Galaxy decompresses it).
**Outputs**
- LCA table: one row per sequence with at least one kept hit: lineage, sequence name, length, number of hits with different taxonomy IDs, identity and coverage of the top hit, the species among the compared hits, the name source, and the read counts per sample. - taxa_raw: up to 10 hits per sequence, one row each, in the FAIRe format. - taxa_final: one row per sequence in the FAIRe format. - hits with no lineage: the BLAST lines that were skipped because no lineage was found (tab-separated).
The job needs no network access: the taxonomy, FishBase and WoRMS files are given to the script as local files.
**Pipeline settings**
The OceanOmics pipeline (ocom profile) runs the script with minimum identity 90, minimum coverage 90, identity window 1 and ranking by bit score.
